citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility did not maintain the foot health of one adult llama.
A VMO observed an adult llama with significantly overgrown toenails on the front and back feet. They were curving
inwards towards the center of the foot, which is an abnormal shape for this species. A representative stated all llamas had
toenail trims in April/May of this year and they intended to trim the nails again once the animals returned from their
temporary exhibition (November).
Overgrown nails can alter gait, which can lead to pain or other foot diseases.
The facility has made arrangements to trim this animal's nails at their temporary exhibition. The facility must use
appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries, and ensure the availability of
emergency, weekend, and holiday care.
Correction date: October 31, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives at Didier farms in Lincolnshire, IL.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
